acceptance.check: Each of the ten weekly end-bound cases runs exactly once across the desktop-client unit suite: no two files execute the same case, and the suite's reportable test count drops by exactly ten relative to main.
acceptance.how_to_verify:
WORKING DIRECTORY: every command below runs inside the checkout under test, as `cd _pr && …`. The repo root is the framework at main and holds a pristine copy of `packages/` — running there reads the UNFIXED tree. The base ref is `origin/main` and never bare `main`, because `_pr` is a detached-HEAD SHA checkout with no local `main` branch.

Static count, which does not need the suite to start. `cd _pr && for f in $(git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets | grep '\.test\.ts$'); do git show origin/main:$f; done | grep -cP "it\('\K"` prints 194 — the nine test files in that directory on main. `cd _pr && grep -hP "it\('\K" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/*.test.ts | wc -l` prints 184 after the change (all nine files are flat in that directory, so the two forms count the same set; after the deletion the glob matches eight files). The difference is exactly ten. Both numbers were run in this checkout and again in the `_pr` layout.

Then the behavioural check, also from `_pr`: `cd _pr && yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vitest run src/components/reports/spreadsheets/ --reporter=verbose`. On main each of the ten titles appears twice, once in each file; after the change each appears exactly once, under the same two describes (`weekly custom report end bound`, `weekly grouped report end bound`) in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts, seven and three, and the passed count is ten lower. No test outside those ten changes result.

acceptance.how_to_verify:
WORKING DIRECTORY: `cd _pr`, base ref `origin/main`. This matters more here than anywhere else: from the repo root the left-hand `git show main:…` reads the copy of weekly-end-date.test.ts that still exists at main, and the right-hand sed reads the survivor at main, which has no comment block — the comparison is then main against main and passes on ANY tree. Inside `_pr` a bare `main` does not resolve at all.

Run this one command, which compares only the weekly end-bound cases rather than the whole file. Two things about it are load-bearing. (1) The pattern is `it\('` — the literal `(` after `it` is REQUIRED. Without it the extraction yields nothing, both sides are empty, and the diff exits 0 on any tree whatsoever. (2) The paths are written out in full, with NO shell variable. With a `D=`/`$D` form, an unset `$D` — which happens if only the `diff` line is copied — makes git and sed error on stderr while `diff` still compares two empty streams and exits 0: the same vacuous pass by a second route.

cd _pr && diff <(git show origin/main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+") \
           <(sed -n "/^describe(.weekly custom report end bound/,/^describe(.weekly budgeted report end bound/p" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+")

It must print nothing, print NOTHING on stderr, and exit 0. Both sides are ten-title lists and they are equal. Sanity-check the pattern before trusting the result: `cd _pr && grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | wc -l` must print 23 for the whole file, and the same pattern piped through the sed range above must print 10. If either prints 0, the pattern has been mangled and the diff is meaningless; the wrong pattern `it'\K[^']+` prints 1 and 0 on those two, and that 0 is what makes the broken version vacuous.

This scoping is deliberate and is not a regression: the whole file holds 23 `it('` titles, and diffing the branch file in full against main's ten prints `10a11,23` plus 13 extra titles and exits 1 even on a correct implementation, because those 13 belong to four describes out_of_scope forbids touching. The right-hand sed range is matched by describe NAME, not by line number, because the inserted comment block shifts every describe by +14 (the `weekly custom report end bound` describe is at 380 on main and 394 after this change). The range ends at the `describe` line itself, so the next describe's cases are excluded.

This check was negative-tested in this run, in the real `_pr` layout, with the exact command text above. On a tree where the entire `weekly grouped report end bound` describe (three of the ten cases) is removed from the survivor it prints `8,10d7` followed by `applies the same bound as the custom spreadsheet`, `clamps to today the same way the custom spreadsheet does` and `widens a week-start end date in the table view too`, and exits 1. On a tree where `clamps to today while the final week is still in progress` is renamed to `clamps to today when the final week is unfinished` inside the survivor it prints `3c3` with both titles and exits 1. On the correct tree it prints nothing on stdout, nothing on stderr, and exits 0. It has teeth in both directions.

If a shell mangles the nested quotes, the equivalent subset form — `cd _pr && comm -23 <(git show origin/main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" | sort) <(grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | sort)` — also prints nothing and exits 0; prefer the diff, because the subset form is one-sided and would not notice a case renamed or added inside the two weekly describes.

Separately, confirm no third file anywhere in the repo carries these titles: `cd _pr && git grep -l -F "it('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed'" origin/main -- packages` names exactly the two files being reconciled, and `cd _pr && git grep -l -F "it('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed'" -- packages` on the edited tree names only custom-spreadsheet.test.ts. Finally, `cd _pr && git diff -U0 origin/main...HEAD -- packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts` shows no removed line (`grep -cE '^-[^- ]|^[-]$'` returns 0), so no assertion inside the ten cases was touched.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the rejected pattern by changing the regex to something that cannot be mis-transcribed, e.g. `grep -oP "it\(?'\K[^']+"` or a `sed -n "s/^\s*it('\(.*\)',.*/\1/p"` form.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: An optional-paren regex silently tolerates the exact omission that caused the earlier rejection — it would match in a file that lacks the parenthesis, which is a different file shape, and it hides a transcription error rather than surfacing it. The `sed` capture form avoids backslashes entirely and is tempting, but it is anchored on `it('` at line start with a specific trailing `',` and would need re-checking against every one of the ten call sites' formatting. The plan keeps the exact corrected pattern AND requires the sanity counts (23 and 10) before the diff is trusted, which is what catches a mis-transcription.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the `D=`/`$D` variable in AC-4 and qa_script step 2 for readability, and rely on the sanity counts alone to catch a mistyped path.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The sanity counts do not catch it. An unset `$D` produces error output on stderr and still exits 0 from the diff, while the sanity count command — which QA may well run with its own correctly-set variable — prints the expected 23 and 10. The check would pass while comparing nothing. Writing both paths out in full removes the failure mode instead of trying to detect it, and the paths are stable: they are named in the delete instruction and in the diff anyway.

Confirm the diff is a deletion plus two small additions. Run inside the checkout under test — the repo root is the framework at main and holds a pristine copy of `packages/`, so a root-addressed diff reads the UNFIXED tree and prints nothing:

cd _pr && git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD

It lists exactly three files: packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts as deleted (338 deletions), custom-spreadsheet.test.ts as modified (14 insertions) and upcoming-release-notes/remove-duplicate-weekly-end-date-suite.md as added. Nothing else. The base ref is `origin/main`, never bare `main`: `_pr` is a detached-HEAD SHA checkout (`git rev-parse --verify main` there returns `fatal: Needed a single revision`), so a bare-`main` command dies rather than reporting anything.

Confirm no case was lost. This step compares ONLY the weekly end-bound cases — do not widen it to the whole file, which holds 23 titles and would fail on a correct implementation. Two things about the command below are load-bearing and both have bitten a previous version of this plan. (a) The pattern is `it\('` — `it`, then a literal open parenthesis, then a quote. Without the parenthesis the extraction returns nothing, both sides are empty, and the diff exits 0 on any tree, including one where cases have been deleted. (b) The paths are written out in full on purpose: do NOT replace them with a `D=` shell variable, because if `$D` is unset git and sed error on stderr while `diff` still compares two empty streams and exits 0. Both defects produced a silently passing check. Run it inside `_pr`, as a single copy-pasteable block:

cd _pr && diff <(git show origin/main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+") \
           <(sed -n "/^describe(.weekly custom report end bound/,/^describe(.weekly budgeted report end bound/p" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+")

BEFORE trusting the result, run `cd _pr && grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | wc -l` — it must print 23 — and the same pattern through the sed range, which must print 10. A 0 or 1 here means the pattern was mangled and the diff below means nothing. Expected from the diff: NO output on stdout, NO output on stderr, exit 0 — both sides are the same ten titles in the same order. This check is known to fail when it should: run in this run's layout, with three of the ten cases removed from the survivor it printed `8,10d7` plus the three missing titles and exited 1, and with one title renamed inside the survivor it printed `3c3` with both titles and exited 1.

The right-hand sed range is matched by describe NAME, not by line number, because the inserted comment block moves `weekly custom report end bound` from line 380 on main to line 394 after the change; a line-numbered range would go stale and silently compare the wrong lines. The range's end pattern matches the `describe('weekly budgeted report end bound'` line itself and stops there, so that describe's cases are excluded. If your shell mangles the nested quotes, `cd _pr && comm -23 <(git show origin/main:packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts | grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" | sort) <(grep -oP "it\('\K[^']+" packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts | sort)` is an equivalent that also prints nothing and exits 0, though it is the weaker check. Confirm separately that no third file carries these titles: `cd _pr && git grep -l -F "it('covers the whole final week once that week has elapsed'" origin/main -- packages` must name exactly the two files being reconciled, and the same grep without the `origin/main --` must name only custom-spreadsheet.test.ts.

Confirm nothing else referenced the deleted file. Run inside the checkout under test:

cd _pr && grep -rn 'weekly-end-date' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=plan --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.mts' --include='*.js' --include='*.jsx' --include='*.json' --include='*.yml' --include='*.yaml' .

Expected output is EXACTLY ONE line, and it is the mandated comment inside the survivor:
`./packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/custom-spreadsheet.test.ts:382:// A second copy of these same ten cases lived in weekly-end-date.test.ts,`
Anything else on stdout — another path, or a second hit in that file — is a failure. There is no trailing `grep -v`, so a run with the expected line prints exit 0.

This command is deliberately addressed to `_pr` and deliberately carries NO `--exclude` flags for work-order.json, plan-review.json or previous-output.json. That is a change from the previous version and it is the point of this step. Those files are written to the REPO ROOT, not into `_pr`, so from inside the checkout under test they are not there to exclude — verified in this run's layout, where the same grep from `_pr` with no excludes at all returns exactly the one expected line. The previous version's three `--exclude` flags were load-bearing under GNU grep's last-one-wins rule (a later `--include='*.json'` re-admits work-order.json if the exclude comes first), and that ordering hazard is now removed rather than documented. The `--include` list is why the mandated comment's own hit is the only thing this can see: the release note's `.md` filename is not in the list, so no exemption list has to be kept in step anywhere.

Do not run this from the repo root. Measured in this run's layout, the identical command from the root returns TWO hits — a hit in the framework's own `./work-order.json` and, via the `_pr/` directory nested inside it, the same comment under an `_pr/` prefix — because the root holds a full copy of `packages/` at main. `plan/` is likewise a pipeline directory that exists only at the root; the `--exclude-dir=plan` flag is kept as harmless defence but is not needed from inside `_pr`.

residual_risks: The vitest halves of AC-1 and AC-5 are the only claims here not directly executed, because this checkout has no node_modules state and vitest cannot start. Both are stated as measurements to take against main. The static half of AC-1 — 194 `it('` titles across the directory on main, 184 after — was executed here and needs no suite.

A QA agent who retypes AC-4's command from memory rather than copying it could reintroduce either vacuous-pass fault (a mangled pattern, or an unset path). The required sanity counts (23 and 10) catch the first; the second is removed by writing the paths in full rather than mitigated.

The `cd _pr &&` prefix is repeated in every command and is the single most likely thing to be dropped when a step is paraphrased. Dropping it does not fail loudly — the root has a working copy of `packages/`, so the command still runs and still exits 0 on the unfixed tree. This is why the reason is restated in each acceptance criterion and each qa_script step rather than stated once.
risks: The one real risk is a silent coverage loss if the diff were read only at the title level. It was not, and the evidence is stronger this run than last: a whitespace-insensitive diff of the two describe blocks (`diff -w -B`) shows every difference is the `runCustom({...})` against `runCustom(weeklyProps({...}))` wrapper and nothing else, the 77 changed lines contain zero assertion lines, the `weeklyProps` defaults are exactly the defaults the deleted file's own `runCustom` supplied, the 7/3 describe split is the same in both files, and the weeklyRows fixture is md5-identical (6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 both sides). AC-4 carries the exact command that proves the titles survived, and that command was run in the failing direction before the passing one in the real QA layout: it reports three missing titles and exits 1 when cases are removed from the survivor, and reports a renamed title and exits 1 when one is renamed. AC-4 also requires two sanity counts — 23 for the whole file and 10 for the scoped range — before the diff is trusted, because two different transcription faults (a mangled pattern, an unset `$D`) each make the diff vacuously pass. That command is SCOPED to the two weekly describes, and the scoping is deliberate: the unscoped whole-file form was measured and prints `10a11,23` plus 13 titles and exits 1 on a correct implementation. No criterion in this work order compares whole-file title lists.

A wrong working directory or base ref is now the dominant failure mode, and it is the one v6 got wrong. Every command is prefixed `cd _pr &&` and every base ref is `origin/main`, and the reason is stated in each artefact rather than once. A command run from the repo root silently compares pristine main against pristine main and exits 0 on any tree whatsoever — that was proven in this run by checking that the root holds its own copy of the deleted file. A command run from `_pr` with a bare `main` does not silently pass; it dies with `fatal: bad revision 'main'`, which is the safe failure. The two failure modes are not symmetric, which is why the bare-`main` form is also forbidden even though it cannot produce a false pass.

The blank line between the comment block and the `describe` is the one thing easy to get wrong. Omit it and the block's last line sits directly above the `describe`. files[1] and AC-2 both state the resulting line numbers (380-392 block, 393 blank, 394 describe) and the added-line count (14, not 13) so that omission is caught by the diff rather than argued about.

The comment text is mandated verbatim because a paraphrase is what made v2 unsatisfiable. If the implementer rewords it, AC-2 fails. If a future reviewer finds the wording wrong, change files[1] and AC-2 in the same edit.

The survivor's server double is stricter than the deleted file's — it applies the `$transform` precision and splits the amount filter, which the shorter file did not. This changes nothing for these ten cases (every weeklyRows amount is positive and the interval is Weekly), and the survivor is where these tests already run and pass today, but it is why this file is the copy to delete. The survivor's double reads its rows through a mutable `servedRows` indirection that the deleted file did not have, reset in `afterEach`; that is a property of the shared double, not of the ten cases.

The category fixtures in the two files are the same two objects under different const names (`categories`/`categoryGroups` in the deleted file, `weeklyCategories`/`weeklyCategoryGroups` in the survivor), so a whole-file diff does not pair them up. They are replaced by name and are referenced by value, and their contents are identical — verified by reading both blocks. Their helpers have no behaviour of their own.

Any command in this work order that locates a describe by line number will go stale after the insertion, because the block moves every describe from line 380 onward by +14. That is why qa_script step 2 and AC-4 match on the describe NAME. Line numbers quoted anywhere in this work order are stated as pre-change values except where they are explicitly given as post-change values.
No new hosts are contacted by this change and no data is sent anywhere, so env.api_allowlist in .sdlc/config.yml needs no addition. Nothing in forbidden_paths is touched.

The implementer must not be tempted to also delete or merge the other describes in custom-spreadsheet.test.ts (weekly budgeted, category axis narrowing, 'any of', text operators — at 551, 644, 802, 954 on main and 565, 658, 816, 968 after this change). They are not duplicates and are out of scope.

work_order.understanding: The weekly end-bound suite exists twice and runs twice. packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/weekly-end-date.test.ts is 338 lines with 10 `it(...)`; custom-spreadsheet.test.ts is 1100 lines and carries all ten of those titles under `weekly custom report end bound` (line 380 on main, seven cases) and `weekly grouped report end bound` (line 504 on main, three cases). v6 was rejected on one objection and the objection is correct and mechanical, not substantive: every verification command was addressed to the repository root and to a bare `main`, but .github/workflows/sdlc-qa.yml checks the commit under test out at `path: _pr` with `ref: <sha>` and `fetch-depth: 0`, while the root is a separate checkout of the framework at main that contains its own full copy of `packages/` — the deleted file is still sitting there. The QA prompt says of the root: 'do not read the app from it, it is the WRONG commit.' `_pr` is checked out by SHA, so it is a detached HEAD with no local `main`, only `refs/remotes/origin/main`. The failure is therefore exhaustive: from the root every command reads pristine main; from `_pr` every bare-`main` command dies with 'fatal: bad revision'. I reproduced the whole layout in this run — a root clone at main containing `_pr` fetched from it and checked out detached at the SHA — and confirmed each half. This version rewrites every command as `cd _pr && …` with `origin/main` as the base ref, and every one of them was executed in that layout. The technical finding is unchanged and was re-derived from scratch: the ten titles are byte-identical between the files, a whitespace-insensitive diff of the two describe blocks shows every single difference is the `runCustom({...})` against `runCustom(weeklyProps({...}))` wrapper, and `weeklyProps`' defaults (startDate 2026-08-30, interval Weekly, firstDayOfWeekIdx '0', the same two category fixtures, groupBy 'Category') are exactly the defaults the deleted file's own `runCustom` supplied. So the epic's 'fold back whatever it uniquely adds' resolves one way: the 338-line file contributes nothing unique and is deleted outright. One correction to v6's numbers, found by re-measuring with the right sed boundaries: v6 said 76 changed lines in the describe-block diff and its own range stopped short, so my first attempt at 380-551 also cut the block in half and surfaced two 'differing' assertion lines that were an artefact of my truncation, not a real difference. With the range ending at the line before `weekly budgeted report end bound` the true figure is 77 changed lines of which ZERO contain an assertion, and the two `groupedLast.intervalEndDate` expectations v6 and I both briefly thought had vanished are present in both files at survivor lines 530-531, 545-546 and 560-561. The weeklyRows fixture is md5-identical (6342ab83b4f60f70b3f77d129ec0d601 both sides) and the 7/3 describe split holds in both files.

It does not affect the decision — the duplication is present on main either way, which is what the diff shows.
